The Thirsty Crow

Once there was a crow. One hot summer day it became very thirsty. It flew here and there in search of water but found none. At last it saw a pitcher in a garden. It flew down and found a little water at the bottom of the pitcher. But the water was so low that the crow could not reach it.

Moral: Where there is a will, there is a way.

Unity is Strength

One day he called his sons and gave them a bundle of sticks. He asked each of them to break the bundle. One by one they tried with all their strength, but none could break it. Then the old man untied the bundle and gave each son a single stick. This time they broke the sticks very easily.

The old man said, 'My sons, if you remain united like the bundle, no one can harm you. But if you quarrel, your enemies will break you easily.' The sons understood their mistake and promised to live in unity.

Moral: Unity is strength.

The Ant and the Dove

Once an ant went to a river to drink water. While drinking, it suddenly slipped and fell into the water. The current began to carry it away, and the ant struggled hard to save its life. A dove was sitting on a tree by the river. Seeing the danger of the ant, the kind dove plucked a leaf and dropped it near the ant. The ant quickly climbed onto the leaf and floated to the bank. Thus its life was saved.

A few days later, a hunter came to the river to catch birds. He saw the dove and aimed his gun at it. The ant noticed this and wanted to save its friend. It crawled up and bit the hunter hard on the foot. The hunter cried out in pain, and his gun missed the aim. At once the dove flew away and saved its life.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A greedy dog — got a piece of meat — crossed a bridge — saw its shadow in water — thought it another dog with meat — barked to snatch it — lost its own meat.
data.model_answer_en:
The Greedy Dog

Once a dog was very hungry. It searched here and there for food. At last it found a piece of meat in a butcher's shop. It took the meat in its mouth and ran to a lonely place to eat it. On the way it had to cross a narrow bridge over a river. As it was crossing the bridge, it looked down and saw its own shadow in the water. The foolish dog thought that it was another dog with a piece of meat. It became greedy and wanted to snatch that piece too. So it barked at the shadow with its mouth open. As soon as it opened its mouth, its own piece of meat fell into the water and was lost for ever. The greedy dog now repented, but it was too late.

Moral: Grasp all, lose all.

data.model_answer_en:
The Fox and the Crow

Once a crow stole a piece of cheese from a window. It flew up and sat on the branch of a tree to eat it. Just then a hungry fox was passing by. It saw the cheese in the crow's beak and wanted to get it. The fox was very cunning. It came under the tree and began to praise the crow. 'What a beautiful bird you are!' it said. 'Your voice must be as sweet as your looks. Please sing a song for me.' The foolish crow was pleased at this flattery. To show its sweet voice, it opened its beak to sing. At once the piece of cheese fell down from its beak. The clever fox caught it and ran away, laughing at the foolish crow.

Moral: Beware of flatterers.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: An old man — had four lazy sons — before death — told them a treasure was hidden in the field — after his death — sons dug the field — found no treasure — but got a good harvest.
data.model_answer_en:
The Hidden Treasure

Once there lived an old farmer in a village. He had four sons who were very lazy. They never worked and always quarrelled among themselves. The old man was very worried about their future. When he was about to die, he called his sons to his bedside. He told them that he had hidden a treasure somewhere in his field. After his death the sons wanted to get the treasure quickly. They took spades and dug the whole field very carefully. But they found no treasure anywhere. They were disappointed. As the field had been dug well, one of them advised sowing seeds in it. They did so. In time the field gave them a rich harvest. Then they understood the real meaning of their father's words.

Moral: Industry is the key to success.

data.model_answer_en:
The Hare and the Tortoise

Once there lived a hare and a tortoise in a forest. The hare was very proud of its speed. It often made fun of the tortoise for its slow movement. One day the tortoise felt hurt and challenged the hare to a race. The hare laughed and agreed. The race began. The hare ran very fast and soon left the tortoise far behind. Feeling sure of its victory, the hare thought of taking a short rest. It lay down under a tree and soon fell asleep. Meanwhile the tortoise kept walking slowly but steadily. It passed the sleeping hare and reached the goal. When the hare woke up and ran to the goal, it found that the tortoise had already won the race. The hare was ashamed of its pride.

Moral: Slow and steady wins the race.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A fox — was very hungry — saw ripe grapes on a high vine — jumped again and again — could not reach them — went away saying the grapes were sour.
data.model_answer_en:
The Fox and the Grapes

One hot summer day a fox was walking through a garden. It was very hungry and was looking for food. Suddenly it saw a bunch of ripe grapes hanging from a high vine. The grapes looked juicy and sweet. The fox's mouth watered at the sight. It wanted to eat the grapes at any cost. So it jumped up to reach them, but it failed. It jumped again and again with all its might, yet it could not reach the grapes, for they were too high. At last the fox became tired and gave up trying. But it did not want to admit its failure. So, walking away, it said to itself, 'The grapes are sour. They are not worth eating.'

Moral: The grapes are sour to those who cannot reach them.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: An old man — a bundle of sticks — his sons always quarrelled — asked each to break the whole bundle — none could — then broke the sticks one by one easily — taught them unity.
data.model_answer_en:
Unity Is Strength

Once there lived an old man in a village. He had several sons. They loved one another, but they often quarrelled among themselves. The old man was very unhappy to see this. He wanted to teach them the value of unity. One day he called all his sons and gave them a bundle of sticks. He asked each of them to break the whole bundle. One by one they tried their best, but none of them could break it. Then the old man untied the bundle and gave each son a single stick. He asked them to break it. This time each of them broke the stick very easily. The old man said, 'If you remain united like the bundle, no one can harm you. But if you are divided, your enemies will break you easily.' The sons understood the lesson.

Moral: Unity is strength.

data.model_answer_en:
The Honest Woodcutter

Once there lived a poor woodcutter. He earned his living by cutting wood in a forest near a river. One day he was cutting a tree on the bank of the river. Suddenly his axe slipped from his hand and fell into the deep water. He had no other axe, so he sat on the bank and began to weep. At this a water fairy appeared before him. She dived into the water and brought up a golden axe. She asked if it was his. The honest woodcutter said, 'No.' Then she brought up a silver axe, but again he said it was not his. At last she brought up his own iron axe. The woodcutter cried out with joy, 'Yes, this is my axe.' The fairy was pleased with his honesty and gave him all three axes as a reward.

Moral: Honesty is the best policy.

data.model_answer_en:
The Fox and the Goat

Once a fox fell into a deep well. The water in it was low, so the fox did not drown, but it could not get out anyhow. It tried again and again, yet it failed. After some time a thirsty goat came to the well in search of water. It saw the fox inside and asked whether the water was good. The cunning fox hid its trouble and said, 'The water is very sweet and cool. Come down and drink to your heart's content.' The foolish goat believed the fox and at once jumped into the well. When the goat had drunk enough, the fox said, 'Let us think how to get out.' Then the clever fox climbed up on the goat's back and jumped out of the well. It left the poor goat inside and ran away.

Moral: Look before you leap.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: King Bruce — defeated many times — hid in a cave — saw a spider trying to reach the ceiling — it failed six times — succeeded the seventh time — the king took heart and won.
data.model_answer_en:
Try Again

Robert Bruce was the king of Scotland. He fought many battles against the English to free his country. But he was defeated again and again. At last he lost all hope and hid himself in a lonely cave. One day, as he was lying in the cave, he saw a spider trying to reach the ceiling by its web. The spider tried to climb up but fell down. It tried a second time, a third time and so on, but each time it failed. Bruce counted that the spider had failed six times. Yet it did not give up. On the seventh try, the spider at last reached the ceiling. This sight gave Bruce new hope and courage. He came out of the cave, gathered his soldiers again and fought against the enemy. This time he defeated them and freed his country.

Moral: If at first you don't succeed, try, try again.

data.model_answer_en:
A Friend in Need

Once two friends were passing through a forest. They had promised to help each other in times of danger. Suddenly a big bear appeared before them. One of the friends was selfish. He at once climbed up a tree to save himself, without thinking of his friend. The other friend did not know how to climb. He was in great danger. But he had heard that a bear does not touch a dead body. So he lay down on the ground and held his breath like a dead man. The bear came near him and smelt his ears and nose. Taking him for dead, it went away. Then the first friend came down and asked what the bear had whispered in his ear. The other replied, 'The bear has told me not to trust a selfish friend.'

Moral: A friend in need is a friend indeed.

data.model_answer_en:
The Shepherd Boy and the Wolf

Once there was a shepherd boy in a village. Every day he took his sheep to a field to graze. The field was far from the village, and the boy often felt lonely and bored. One day, just for fun, he cried out loudly, 'Wolf! Wolf!' Hearing his cry, the villagers ran to the field with sticks to save the sheep. But they found no wolf and returned home angrily. The boy laughed at them. He played the same trick a few more times, and each time the villagers were fooled. A few days later a real wolf attacked the flock. The frightened boy cried out, 'Wolf! Wolf!' with all his might. But this time the villagers thought it was another false alarm, so nobody came to help him. The wolf killed and ate many of his sheep.

Moral: A liar is not believed even when he tells the truth.

data.model_answer_en:
The Thirsty Crow

One hot summer day a crow felt very thirsty. It flew here and there in search of water, but it could not find any. At last it saw a jar in a garden. The crow flew down to the jar and found a little water at the bottom. But the water was so low that it could not reach it with its beak. It tried again and again but failed. The crow did not lose heart. Suddenly a clever plan came to its mind. It saw some small pebbles lying nearby. The crow began to drop the pebbles into the jar one by one. As the pebbles went in, the water slowly rose up. When the water came near the mouth of the jar, the crow drank it to its heart's content. Then it flew away happily.

Moral: Where there is a will, there is a way.

data.model_answer_en:
The Camel and the Jackal

Once a camel and a jackal were friends. One day the jackal said, 'I know a field full of sweet crops across the river. Let us go there.' The camel agreed and carried the jackal across the river on its back. They reached the field and began to eat. The jackal soon finished its little meal, but the camel was still eating. Then the jackal started to howl loudly. Hearing the howl, the villagers came running with sticks and beat the poor camel badly. When they left, the camel asked the jackal why it had howled so early. The jackal cleverly replied that it had a habit of howling after a meal. On the way back, the camel took the jackal on its back. In the middle of the river the camel dived into the water, and the jackal was washed away.

Moral: Tit for tat.

The Ant and the Dove

Once an ant went to a river to drink water. While drinking, it slipped and fell into the water. The current began to carry it away, and the ant struggled hard for its life. A dove was sitting on a tree by the river. Seeing the danger of the ant, the kind dove plucked a leaf and dropped it near the ant. The ant quickly climbed onto the leaf and floated to the bank. Thus its life was saved. A few days later a hunter came to the river. He saw the dove sitting on the tree and aimed his gun at it. The ant noticed this and wanted to save its friend. It quickly crawled up and bit the hunter hard on the foot. The hunter cried out in pain, and his gun missed the aim. At once the dove flew away and saved its life.

Moral: One good turn deserves another.

data.model_answer_en:
The Lion and the Mouse

Once a lion was sleeping in a forest. A little mouse was playing nearby. By chance it ran over the body of the lion. The lion woke up in anger and caught the mouse in its paw. The frightened mouse begged for mercy. It said, 'Please forgive me this time, sir. If you set me free, I may help you some day.' The lion laughed at the idea that such a tiny creature could help him. But he took pity on the mouse and let it go. Some days later the lion was caught in a hunter's net. It roared loudly but could not free itself. The mouse heard the roar and came running. It cut the net with its sharp teeth and set the lion free. The lion was grateful to the little mouse.

Moral: Do not hate anyone as weak or small.

data.model_answer_en:
The Goose That Laid Golden Eggs

Once a farmer had a wonderful goose. Every morning the goose laid a golden egg. The farmer sold the eggs in the market and slowly became rich. But he was very greedy. He was not satisfied with one egg a day. He thought that there must be a heap of gold inside the goose. He wanted to get all the gold at once. So one day he killed the goose and cut open its body to take out the gold. But to his surprise, he found nothing inside. It was just like any other goose. Now he had neither the gold nor the golden eggs. His greed had ruined him completely. He repented for his foolishness, but it was too late.

Moral: Greed is a curse.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A milkmaid — carrying a pot of milk on her head — dreaming of profit — planning to buy eggs, chickens and a dress — nodded her head in joy — the pot fell down — all her dreams were broken.
data.model_answer_en:
Do Not Count Your Chickens Before They Are Hatched

Once a milkmaid was going to the market to sell a pot of milk. She was carrying the pot on her head. As she walked along, she began to build castles in the air. She thought, 'With the money from this milk, I shall buy some eggs. The eggs will give me chickens. I shall sell the chickens and buy a beautiful dress. Wearing that dress, I shall go to the fair. Many young men will look at me, but I shall proudly toss my head and refuse them all.' Thinking this, she really tossed her head in joy. At once the pot of milk fell down from her head and broke. All the milk was spilt on the ground. With the milk, all her sweet dreams were also broken.

Moral: Do not build castles in the air.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A cap seller — slept under a tree — a group of monkeys took his caps — he woke up and saw them wearing caps — he threw his own cap down in anger — the monkeys copied him — he got back all his caps.
data.model_answer_en:
The Cap Seller and the Monkeys

Once there was a cap seller. He used to sell caps from village to village. One hot afternoon he felt very tired. He put down his basket of caps and lay down under a big tree to take rest. Soon he fell fast asleep. There were many monkeys on the tree. They came down, took the caps from the basket and put them on their heads. Then they climbed up the tree again. When the cap seller woke up, he found his basket empty. Looking up, he saw the monkeys wearing his caps. He shouted and made faces at them, but the monkeys only imitated him. At last, in anger, he threw his own cap on the ground. At once the monkeys also threw down their caps in imitation. The clever cap seller quickly gathered all his caps and went away happily.

Moral: Wisdom wins where force fails.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: The sun and the wind — quarrelled about who was stronger — a traveller came — they agreed to test on him — the wind blew hard but the man held his coat tight — the sun shone warmly — the man took off his coat — the sun won.
data.model_answer_en:
The Sun and the Wind

Once the sun and the wind had a quarrel. Each of them claimed to be stronger than the other. Just then they saw a traveller walking along the road with a coat on. They agreed that the one who could make the traveller take off his coat would be the stronger. First the wind took its turn. It began to blow very hard and cold. But the harder the wind blew, the more tightly the traveller wrapped his coat around him. At last the wind gave up. Then it was the sun's turn. The sun came out and began to shine gently and warmly. Slowly the day grew hot. The traveller began to sweat. Feeling too hot, he took off his coat at once. Thus the sun won the contest.

Moral: Gentleness can do what force cannot.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: Bayazid Bostami — his mother felt thirsty at night — asked for water — he brought water — she had fallen asleep — he stood by her bed holding the glass all night.
data.model_answer_en:
A Devoted Son

Bayazid Bostami was a great Muslim saint. He loved and served his mother very much. One night his mother fell ill and felt very thirsty. She asked Bayazid for a glass of water. Bayazid at once went to fetch water. But when he came back with the water, he found that his mother had fallen asleep. He did not want to wake her from her sleep. So he stood silently by her bed, holding the glass of water in his hand. He waited there patiently for his mother to wake up. In this way he passed the whole night standing without any rest. When his mother woke up in the early morning, she was greatly moved to see her devoted son. She gave him her heartfelt blessings.

Moral: Service to mother is a great virtue.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A donkey — put on a lion's skin — frightened all the animals — brayed loudly out of pride — the fox knew it by its voice — the donkey was caught and beaten.
data.model_answer_en:
The Donkey in the Lion's Skin

Once a donkey found the skin of a dead lion in a forest. A foolish idea came into its mind. It put on the lion's skin and began to move about in the forest. Seeing the shape of a lion, all the animals ran away in fear. The donkey was very pleased to see this. It enjoyed frightening the other animals for some days. It became very proud of itself. One day, out of pride, it began to bray loudly. A clever fox was passing by. As soon as it heard the sound, it understood that it was only a donkey and not a lion. The fox said, 'I would have been afraid too, if I had not heard your voice.' Soon the other animals also came to know the truth. They caught the donkey and gave it a good beating.

Moral: Pride goes before a fall.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A wolf — drinking water upstream — a lamb drinking downstream — the wolf blamed the lamb for muddying the water — the lamb proved it impossible — the wolf made more false charges — at last killed the lamb.
data.model_answer_en:
The Wolf and the Lamb

One day a wolf was drinking water at a stream. A little lamb was also drinking water lower down the same stream. The wolf was hungry and wanted to eat the lamb. So it looked for an excuse to quarrel. The wolf said angrily, 'How dare you make the water muddy while I am drinking?' The lamb humbly replied, 'Sir, how can I make the water muddy? You are up the stream and I am far below you. The water flows from you to me.' The wolf could not answer this. Then it brought another false charge, saying that the lamb had spoken ill of it last year. The lamb said it was not even born then. The wolf grew more angry and said, 'Then it was your father.' Saying this, it fell upon the poor lamb and killed it.

Moral: A tyrant never wants an excuse.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: Two cats — found a piece of bread — quarrelled over the share — went to a monkey — the monkey divided it into two — ate from the bigger part again and again — at last ate almost all.
data.model_answer_en:
Two Cats and a Monkey

Once two cats stole a piece of bread. They wanted to share it, but each wanted the bigger part. So they began to quarrel. At last they went to a monkey to settle the matter. The clever monkey agreed to help them. It broke the bread into two pieces. But it made one piece bigger than the other on purpose. Then it said that the pieces were not equal. To make them equal, it took a bite from the bigger piece. Now the other piece became bigger, so it took a bite from that one. In this way the monkey went on biting from each piece, one after another. The two foolish cats watched helplessly. At last only a tiny bit of bread was left. The monkey put it into its own mouth and ran away. The cats got nothing.

Moral: When two quarrel, a third gains.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A jackal — fell into a dyer's tub — its body turned blue — the other animals took it for a king — it ruled proudly — one night it howled — the animals knew it was a jackal — drove it away.
data.model_answer_en:
The Blue Jackal

Once a hungry jackal came into a town in search of food. Some dogs began to chase it. To save itself, the jackal jumped into a dyer's tub full of blue dye. When it came out, its whole body had turned blue. The jackal then ran back to the forest. Seeing its strange blue colour, all the animals were frightened. They had never seen such a creature before. The cunning jackal took the chance. It told the animals that God had sent it to be their king. The foolish animals believed it and made it their king. The blue jackal began to rule proudly and made even the lions and tigers serve it. But one night it heard other jackals howling. Forgetting itself, it also began to howl loudly. At once the animals understood that it was only a jackal. They fell upon it and drove it away.

Moral: Pretence does not last long.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A lion in a forest — killed animals daily — the animals made a deal to send one animal each day — one day a clever rabbit's turn — it came late — told the lion of another lion in a well — the lion looked into the well — jumped in and died.
data.model_answer_en:
The Lion and the Clever Rabbit

Once there lived a fierce lion in a forest. Every day it killed many animals for food. The animals were in great fear. So they made a deal with the lion. They promised to send one animal to it every day, if it stopped killing so many. The lion agreed. One day it was the turn of a little rabbit. The clever rabbit came to the lion very late and on purpose. The lion roared in anger and asked why it was late. The rabbit humbly said that another lion had stopped it on the way and claimed to be the king. Hearing this, the proud lion became furious. It asked the rabbit to show that other lion. The rabbit led it to a deep well and asked it to look inside. The lion saw its own reflection in the water and took it for a rival. In anger it jumped into the well and was drowned.

Moral: Wisdom is better than strength.

data.model_answer_en:
The Astrologer

Once there lived an astrologer in a town. He claimed that he could read the future by looking at the stars. Many people came to him to know their fortunes, and he earned a lot of money by telling them. He was very proud of his knowledge. One clear night the astrologer was walking along a road. As usual, he was gazing up at the stars to read the future. He was so busy looking at the sky that he did not notice the ground before him. Suddenly he fell into a deep pit on the road. He cried out for help, and some people came and pulled him out. When they heard how he had fallen, they laughed at him. One of them said, 'You claim to read the stars in the sky, but you cannot even see the pit at your feet.'

Moral: Look before you leap.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A grateful lion — a thorn in its paw — a slave named Androcles pulled it out — later the slave was thrown before the lion in an arena — the lion did not harm him — recognised its friend.
data.model_answer_en:
Androcles and the Lion

Long ago there lived a slave named Androcles. He was treated cruelly by his master, so one day he ran away to a forest. There he saw a lion lying and groaning in pain. Androcles was frightened at first, but he saw that the lion was helpless. A big thorn had gone into its paw. Bravely, Androcles went near and pulled out the thorn. The lion felt relieved and licked his hand like a friend. From that day they lived together in the forest. After some time Androcles was caught and brought back to his master. As a punishment, he was thrown into an arena before a hungry lion. But when the lion rushed forward, it suddenly stopped. It was the same lion he had helped. Instead of attacking him, the lion began to lick his feet. Everyone was amazed, and Androcles was set free.

Moral: Kindness never goes unrewarded.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A fox — lost its tail in a trap — felt ashamed — advised all foxes to cut off their tails — an old fox understood the trick — asked why — exposed its selfish motive.
data.model_answer_en:
The Fox Without a Tail

Once a fox was caught in a trap. After a hard struggle it managed to escape, but it lost its tail in the trap. Now the fox felt very much ashamed of its ugly look. It did not want to be the only fox without a tail. So it thought of a clever plan. It called a meeting of all the foxes. In the meeting it said, 'Dear friends, our tails are quite useless. They only add to our weight and get dirty. So I think we should all cut off our tails. It will make us look smart.' Most of the foxes were about to agree. But an old and wise fox stood up and said, 'Friend, you are giving us this advice only because you have lost your own tail. You want us to lose ours too.' Hearing this, all the foxes understood the trick and refused to cut their tails.

Moral: Beware of selfish advice.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A king — wanted everything he touched to turn into gold — his wish was granted — his food and even his daughter turned to gold — he repented — prayed to undo the wish.
data.model_answer_en:
The Golden Touch

Long ago there lived a king named Midas. He was very rich, but he was greedy for gold. One day a god appeared before him and offered to grant him a wish. Midas asked that everything he touched might turn into gold. His wish was granted. At first Midas was very happy. He touched the trees, the stones and the chairs, and they all became gold. But soon his joy turned into sorrow. When he sat down to eat, the food and water also turned into gold as soon as he touched them. He could neither eat nor drink. Worse still, when his little daughter ran to him and he embraced her, she too turned into a lifeless golden statue. Midas was broken-hearted. He prayed to the god to take back the fatal gift. The god took pity on him and undid the wish.

Moral: Greed brings misery.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A boy — put his hand into a jar of nuts — grabbed as many as he could — could not pull his hand out — cried — a man advised him to take fewer — he did and got his hand out.
data.model_answer_en:
The Boy and the Nuts

Once a little boy was very fond of nuts. One day he saw a jar full of nuts on a table. The mouth of the jar was rather narrow. The greedy boy put his hand into the jar and grabbed as big a handful of nuts as he could. But when he tried to pull his hand out, he could not. His fist full of nuts was too big to pass through the narrow mouth of the jar. He did not want to drop any of the nuts, so his hand remained stuck. The boy began to cry in despair. Just then a wise man came near and saw his trouble. He said, 'My child, do not be so greedy. Take only half that quantity, and you will easily get your hand out.' The boy followed his advice. He let go of half the nuts, and at once his hand came out.

Moral: Do not be greedy.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A merchant's ass — carried salt across a river — fell into water — the salt melted and the load became light — it fell down on purpose next time — the master loaded it with sponges — the load became heavier — the ass learnt a lesson.
data.model_answer_en:
The Ass and the Load of Salt

Once a merchant had an ass. Every day the ass carried heavy loads for its master. One day it was carrying a load of salt across a river. While crossing the river, the ass slipped and fell into the water. Some of the salt melted in the water, and so the load became much lighter. The ass was very pleased. It thought it had found a clever trick. The next day, while crossing the river with another load of salt, it fell into the water on purpose. Again the salt melted and the load became light. But the master understood the trick of the ass. The next day he loaded the ass with bundles of sponges instead of salt. As usual, the cunning ass fell into the water on purpose. But this time the sponges soaked up a lot of water, and the load became far heavier. The ass suffered greatly and learnt its lesson.

Moral: Cunning tricks bring their own punishment.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A crow — wanted to look beautiful — picked up peacock feathers — stuck them on its body — joined the peacocks — they pulled out the borrowed feathers — the crows also rejected it.
data.model_answer_en:
The Vain Crow

Once there lived a crow. It was not happy with its own black colour and plain look. It always wished to be as beautiful as a peacock. One day it found some bright peacock feathers lying on the ground. A foolish idea came into its mind. It picked up the feathers and stuck them all over its body. Now the crow thought that it looked just like a peacock. Feeling very proud, it left its own kind and went to join a group of peacocks. But the peacocks soon found out the truth. They became angry at the crow's pretence. They fell upon it and pulled out all the borrowed feathers. The poor crow was driven away. Ashamed, it went back to the other crows. But they too refused to accept it because it had insulted its own kind.

Moral: Borrowed feathers do not make one great.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A thirsty pigeon — saw a picture of water on a signboard — thought it real — flew fast towards it — struck the board — fell down and was hurt.
data.model_answer_en:
The Thirsty Pigeon

One hot summer day a pigeon felt very thirsty. It flew here and there in search of water. But it could not find any water anywhere. The heat was unbearable, and the pigeon was almost dying of thirst. At last it saw a big signboard on the roadside. On the board there was the picture of a glass full of water. The foolish pigeon thought that it was real water. Without thinking for a moment, it flew straight towards the board at a great speed. It wanted to drink the water quickly. But as soon as it reached the board, it struck against it with great force. The poor pigeon was badly hurt and fell down on the ground. It lay there groaning in pain. Its hasty action brought about its own ruin.

Moral: Look before you leap.

data.model_answer_en:
The Dove and the Mouse

Once a dove and a mouse were good friends. The dove lived on a tree, and the mouse lived in a hole under the same tree. They loved each other very much. One day the dove went out in search of food. Suddenly it got caught in a hunter's net that was spread on the ground. The dove struggled hard to free itself, but the more it struggled, the more it got entangled. It began to cry in fear. Hearing the cry of its friend, the mouse came out of its hole at once. It saw the dove caught in the net. Without wasting a moment, the mouse began to cut the net with its sharp teeth. It worked hard and cut through the threads one by one. Soon there was a big hole in the net, and the dove came out free. It thanked its friend and flew away happily.

Moral: A friend in need is a friend indeed.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A frog — small in size — saw a big ox — wanted to be as big — began to blow itself up — swelled more and more — at last burst.
data.model_answer_en:
The Vain Frog

Once there lived a frog in a pond. It lived with its family. One day a big ox came to the pond to drink water. The little frog's children saw the huge ox and were amazed at its size. When the mother frog came back, they told her about the great animal they had seen. The mother frog felt jealous. She was very proud and did not want to believe that any animal could be bigger than herself. So she began to blow herself up to become as big as the ox. She asked her children, 'Is the ox as big as this?' They said, 'No, mother, much bigger.' She blew herself up more and more. Again and again she asked, and each time the children said the ox was still bigger. At last, in her foolish pride, she blew herself up so much that she burst and died.

Moral: Pride goes before a fall.

data.model_answer_en:
The Kind Farmer

Once a traveller was passing through a village. He had walked a long way and was very tired and hungry. Night was coming on, and he needed food and shelter. First he went to the house of a rich man of the village. He requested the rich man to give him some food and a place to sleep. But the rich man was hard-hearted. He rudely refused and drove the traveller away. The poor traveller then went to the hut of a poor farmer nearby. The farmer was not well off, but he had a kind heart. He gladly welcomed the traveller. He shared his simple food with him and gave him a place to sleep for the night. The next morning the traveller thanked the poor farmer from the bottom of his heart. He blessed him and went on his way.

Moral: A kind heart is better than riches.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A woodman — prayed to the forest for a handle for his axe — the trees gave him a branch — he made a handle — then began to cut down all the big trees — the trees repented too late.
data.model_answer_en:
The Woodman and the Trees

Once a woodman came to a forest. He had an axe but no handle for it. Without a handle, the axe was useless to him. So he humbly begged the trees to give him a small branch to make a handle. The trees felt pity for the poor woodman. They thought it was only a small favour. So they gave him a branch of a young tree. The woodman was very pleased. He made a strong handle for his axe with the branch. But as soon as the axe was ready, the woodman began to cut down the big trees of the forest one after another. The trees then understood their foolishness. They had given their own enemy the means to destroy them. But it was too late to repent. Soon the whole forest was laid bare.

Moral: Do not give your enemy a weapon against yourself.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A crow and a peacock — the crow wanted colourful feathers — envied the peacock — a wise bird said the peacock cannot fly high or free like the crow — the crow felt happy with its own life.
data.model_answer_en:
Be Happy With What You Have

Once a crow lived near a garden. One day it saw a peacock spreading its colourful feathers. The crow felt very sad about its own dull black colour. It began to envy the peacock and thought, 'How unlucky I am! The peacock is so beautiful, while I am so ugly.' Just then a wise old bird was sitting nearby. It heard the crow complaining and came near. The wise bird said, 'My friend, it is true that the peacock has beautiful feathers. But because of those heavy feathers, it cannot fly high in the sky. It is often kept in cages for its beauty. But you can fly freely wherever you like, and no one keeps you in a cage. So you are luckier than the peacock.' The crow thought over these words and understood the truth. From that day it stopped complaining and lived happily.

Moral: Contentment is the greatest wealth.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: A greedy man — found a purse of gold — a poor man had lost it — the greedy man claimed it had more coins — the judge gave the purse to the poor man — the greedy man got nothing.
data.model_answer_en:
Greed Never Pays

Once a poor man lost a purse containing a hundred gold coins. He was very sad and announced a reward for anyone who found it. A greedy man found the purse on the road. Instead of returning it honestly, he thought of a trick to keep the whole purse. He went to the poor man and gave back the purse. But then he claimed that the purse had contained two hundred coins, not a hundred, and that the poor man had taken out some. The two men began to quarrel and went to a wise judge. The judge counted the coins and found exactly a hundred. Then he said, 'The purse this man found has a hundred coins. But the lost purse had two hundred coins, as this greedy man says. So they are two different purses. This purse is not his. It will be given to the man who lost a hundred coins.' Thus the honest poor man got his purse, and the greedy man got nothing.

Moral: Greed leads to loss.

data.prompt_en: Write a story using the outline and add a title and a moral: An ungrateful tiger — trapped in a cage — begged a Brahmin to free it — promised not to harm him — once free, it wanted to eat him — a clever jackal tricked the tiger back into the cage.
data.model_answer_en:
The Brahmin and the Tiger

Once a tiger was caught in a cage. A kind Brahmin was passing by. The tiger begged him piteously to open the cage, promising that it would never harm him. Out of pity, the Brahmin opened the cage. But as soon as the tiger came out, it forgot its promise. It said it would eat the Brahmin, for it was very hungry. The Brahmin protested and said it was unfair. They agreed to ask others for judgement. The tree and the road both spoke against the Brahmin. At last a clever jackal came. It pretended not to understand how the big tiger had been inside the small cage. The tiger, to show how, went back into the cage. At once the jackal shut the door and locked it. Thus the ungrateful tiger was trapped again, and the Brahmin's life was saved.

Moral: Ingratitude is a great sin.

data.model_answer_en:
The Dishonest Milkman

Once there lived a milkman in a village. He sold milk in the nearby town. But he was very dishonest. Every day he mixed a lot of water with the milk to earn more money. In this way he cheated his customers for a long time and became rich. With his dishonest earnings, he planned to marry his son with great show. One day he was going to the town, carrying a bag of coins to buy things for the wedding. He had to cross a river by boat. In the middle of the river, the boatman began to sing. In the meantime a monkey on the boat took the bag of coins and climbed to the top of the mast. There it began to throw the coins one by one; some fell into the boat and some into the river. Half of his money sank into the water and was lost. It was the very money he had earned by mixing water with milk.

Moral: Ill got, ill spent.

data.model_answer_en:
The Singing Bird

Once a hunter went into a forest to catch birds. He had a gun with him. After walking for some time, he saw a beautiful little bird sitting on the branch of a tree. He raised his gun and aimed at the bird to shoot it. But just at that moment, the bird began to sing a very sweet song. The song was so lovely that the hunter stood still to listen to it. He forgot everything else. The music touched his heart and softened it. He lowered his gun and kept listening with delight. His cruel wish to kill the bird slowly went away. He thought it would be a great sin to kill such a sweet singer. So he did not shoot. The little bird finished its song and flew away safely into the sky. The hunter went back home with a happy and gentle heart.

Moral: Beauty can soften the hardest heart.

data.prompt_en: Write a paragraph comparing 'Village Life and Town Life' (comparison and contrast).
data.model_answer_en: Village life and town life are different in many ways. The main difference lies in the environment. A village is calm, quiet and full of natural beauty, whereas a town is noisy, crowded and full of smoke. In a village, the air is fresh and pure, but in a town it is often polluted. As regards facilities, town life offers more advantages. Towns have good schools, colleges, hospitals and markets, while villages often lack these facilities. On the other hand, the cost of living is low in a village but very high in a town. People in villages are simple and friendly and help one another, whereas town people are busy and have little time for their neighbours. However, both have their own charms. A village gives peace and a healthy life, while a town gives comfort and opportunities. To sum up, though town life is more comfortable, village life is more peaceful and healthy. A wise person enjoys the good sides of both.

data.prompt_en: Write a paragraph on 'Causes and Effects of Air Pollution' (cause and effect).
data.model_answer_en: Air pollution has become a serious problem in our country. There are several causes behind it. The main cause is the smoke emitted from mills, factories and vehicles. This smoke contains harmful gases that pollute the air. Moreover, the burning of fossil fuels, brick kilns and the reckless cutting of trees also pollute the air. These causes lead to many harmful effects. As a result of air pollution, people suffer from various diseases such as asthma, breathing problems and lung cancer. In addition, polluted air destroys the balance of nature and causes global warming. Because of global warming, the sea level is rising and the climate is changing. If we do not control air pollution now, our future will be in great danger. So, we should plant more trees, use eco-friendly vehicles and control the smoke of factories. Only then can we ensure fresh air and a healthy life.

data.prompt_en: Write a paragraph on 'Causes and Effects of Load-shedding' (cause and effect).
data.model_answer_en: Load-shedding is a common problem in our country. It means the temporary cut of electricity supply. There are several causes of load-shedding. The main cause is that our production of electricity is much less than our demand. Moreover, the wastage of electricity, illegal connections and the system loss also cause load-shedding. As a result of load-shedding, our daily life is greatly hampered. Students cannot study properly at night. Mills and factories cannot run smoothly, so the production falls. Patients in hospitals suffer a lot. Because of frequent load-shedding, valuable electrical goods are often damaged. In the hot summer, load-shedding makes our life miserable. It also affects the economy of the country badly. To reduce load-shedding, we should build more power plants and use electricity carefully. We must not waste electricity and should turn off unnecessary lights and fans. Only then can we get relief from this serious problem.

data.prompt_en: Write a paragraph comparing and contrasting 'Online Class and Offline Class'.
data.model_answer_en: Online class and offline class are two methods of learning, and each has its own advantages and disadvantages. In an offline class, students and teachers sit together in the same room, so students can ask questions directly and get instant answers. An online class, on the other hand, is held over the internet, so students can attend it from home. The biggest difference is about place and cost. Offline classes require students to travel to school, while online classes save both time and travel cost. However, in an offline class students can mix with friends and take part in games and other activities, whereas in an online class they often feel lonely. Moreover, an online class fully depends on electricity and a good internet connection, but an offline class does not. In spite of these differences, both types of class aim at the same goal, that is, spreading education. So, a mixture of online and offline classes can bring the best result for students.

In the present, on the other hand, life has become fast, busy and full of comforts. The biggest difference lies in science and technology. In the past there were no computers, mobile phones or fast vehicles, while today these have made our life easy and comfortable. In terms of communication, people of the past had to wait days for a letter, whereas now we can talk to anyone within a moment. However, the past had some good sides too. People were more honest, healthy and free from tension, while modern people suffer from pollution and stress. In spite of these differences, both ages aim at human welfare. So, we should take the good sides of both the past and the present.

data.prompt_en: Write a paragraph comparing and contrasting 'Solar Energy and Electricity from Fuel'.
data.model_answer_en: Solar energy and electricity from fuel are two important sources of power, but they differ in many ways. Solar energy comes from the sunlight, while electricity from fuel is produced by burning gas, coal or oil. Solar energy is a renewable source that will never run out, whereas fuel is limited and will finish one day. There is a difference in their effect on the environment too. Solar energy is clean and causes no pollution, while burning fuel gives off smoke and harmful gases that pollute the air. In terms of cost, setting up solar panels needs money at first but then gives free power, whereas fuel-based electricity has a continuous cost. On the other hand, solar energy depends on sunlight and cannot be produced at night or on cloudy days, while fuel-based electricity can be produced at any time. In spite of this, solar energy is safer and better for our future. So, we should use more solar energy to save our environment.

A king gives orders and is served by many people, while a farmer works with his own hands from morning till evening. There is a difference in their peace of mind too. A king is often worried about his throne and safety, whereas a farmer, though poor, often sleeps in peace after his day's labour. On the other hand, both a king and a farmer are needed by society. Moreover, trees prevent soil erosion and cause rainfall. They protect us from floods, storms and the greenhouse effect. Without trees, the earth would turn into a desert and life would be impossible. The best time for tree plantation is the month of Ashar and Sraban. Everyone should plant at least one tree. Thus, we can make our country greener, healthier and more beautiful.

data.prompt_en: Write a paragraph about 'Load Shedding' by answering: (a) What is load shedding? (b) Why does it happen? (c) How does it affect students and people? (d) What problems does it create? (e) How can it be reduced?
data.model_answer_en: Load shedding means the sudden stoppage of the supply of electricity for some time. It happens when the demand for electricity is greater than its production. In our country, load shedding is a common problem, especially in summer. There are many reasons behind it, such as system loss, misuse of power and lack of enough power plants. Load shedding causes great sufferings to people of all classes. Students cannot study at night and become worried about their examinations. Factories and mills stop working, so the production of goods falls. Patients in hospitals suffer badly when machines stop. In the darkness, thieves and robbers also get a chance to do their crimes. To reduce load shedding, we should not waste electricity and must use energy-saving bulbs. The government should build more power plants and stop the illegal use of electricity. Only through everyone's awareness can this problem be solved.

data.prompt_en: Write a paragraph about 'The International Mother Language Day' answering: (a) What is it? (b) When is it observed? (c) Why is it important? (d) How is it observed? (e) What does it teach us?
data.model_answer_en: The International Mother Language Day is observed on the 21st of February every year. It is a red-letter day in the history of Bangladesh. On this day in 1952, Salam, Barkat, Rafiq, Jabbar and many others laid down their lives for the honour of our mother tongue, Bangla. They protested against the decision to make Urdu the only state language of Pakistan. In memory of their great sacrifice, UNESCO declared 21st February as the International Mother Language Day in 1999. Now the day is observed all over the world. On this day people go to the Shaheed Minar barefoot early in the morning and place flowers there to show respect to the martyrs. Special programmes are held and the national flag is kept at half-mast. The day teaches us to love our mother tongue and to respect other languages too.

data.prompt_en: Write a paragraph about 'Dengue Fever' answering: (a) What is dengue? (b) How does it spread? (c) What are its symptoms? (d) How is it harmful? (e) How can we prevent it?
data.model_answer_en: Dengue is a fatal fever caused by a virus. It has become a serious health problem in our country in recent years. Dengue fever spreads through the bite of a special kind of mosquito called Aedes. This mosquito breeds in clean and stagnant water and usually bites during the daytime. The symptoms of dengue are high fever, severe headache, pain in the joints and muscles, and sometimes bleeding. In serious cases the number of blood platelets falls dangerously. Dengue is very harmful and may even cause death if not treated in time. However, we can prevent dengue by taking some steps. We should not allow water to collect anywhere near our house. We should keep our surroundings clean and use mosquito nets and sprays. If anyone shows the symptoms, he should see a doctor at once. Public awareness is the best way to prevent dengue.

data.prompt_en: Write a paragraph about 'Digital Bangladesh' answering: (a) What is Digital Bangladesh? (b) What does it mean? (c) How does it help us? (d) In which fields is it used? (e) What is its importance?
data.model_answer_en: Digital Bangladesh is a dream of building a modern country with the help of information and communication technology. It means running all the activities of the state and society digitally. In a Digital Bangladesh people can get almost every service through computers and the internet. It helps us in countless ways. We can pay bills, book tickets and send money sitting at home. Students can learn many things online and attend virtual classes. Digital technology is now used in almost every field. In education, healthcare, agriculture, business and administration, digital services have made our life easy and fast. Government offices provide many services online, which saves our time and reduces corruption. The importance of Digital Bangladesh is very great. It saves time and labour, increases efficiency and connects the country with the wider world. To make this dream fully successful, we should spread computer education and internet facilities to every corner of the country.

data.model_answer_en: A hobby is a favourite work that one does in one's leisure time for pleasure. Different people have different hobbies. My hobby is gardening. I developed this hobby from my childhood. My father had a small garden beside our house, and I used to help him look after it. Gradually I became fond of it and made a garden of my own. In my leisure time I work in my garden with great pleasure. I water the plants, remove the weeds and put fences around them. I have planted many flower plants and some fruit trees in my garden. When the flowers bloom and the fruits ripen, my heart fills with joy. My hobby is very useful to me. It gives me both pleasure and profit. It keeps my body and mind fresh and teaches me the value of work. It also supplies my family with fresh flowers and fruits.

data.prompt_en: Write a paragraph about 'A Railway Station' answering: (a) What is a railway station? (b) How does it look? (c) What is seen there? (d) What happens when a train arrives? (e) How do you feel there?
data.model_answer_en: A railway station is a place where trains stop to take and drop passengers. It is a busy and crowded place. A railway station has one or more platforms with sheds over them. There is a ticket counter, a waiting room, a bookstall and refreshment stalls. Many people are seen there. Some are buying tickets, some are waiting for the train and others are moving up and down. Porters carry the luggage of the passengers. When a train arrives, the whole station becomes busy and noisy. Passengers hurry to get down or get into the train. Hawkers cry out to sell their goods. There is a great rush at the doors of the compartments. After a few minutes the train blows its whistle and leaves the station. I feel a strange excitement whenever I stand at a railway station. The busy scene of a railway station is really interesting to watch.

data.prompt_en: Write a paragraph about 'Female Education' answering: (a) What is female education? (b) Why is it important? (c) What is its present condition? (d) What are the obstacles? (e) What should be done?
data.model_answer_en: Female education means the education of girls and women. It is very important for the development of a nation. Women are half of our total population. If they remain uneducated, half of the nation stays backward, and the country cannot go forward. An educated woman can earn her living and help her family. Above all, an educated mother can bring up her children in a proper way. In the past female education was much neglected in our country, but the present condition is much better. Nowadays girls are going to schools and colleges in large numbers, and many of them are doing very well. Still there are some obstacles, such as poverty, early marriage, superstition and social prejudice. To remove these obstacles, we must build public awareness. The government should provide free education and stipends for girls. Then female education will spread, and our nation will surely prosper.

data.prompt_en: Write a paragraph about 'A Rickshaw Puller' answering: (a) Who is a rickshaw puller? (b) How does he live? (c) What does he do? (d) What problems does he face? (e) How useful is he?
data.model_answer_en: A rickshaw puller is a familiar figure in our towns and cities. He is a poor man who earns his living by pulling a rickshaw. He generally lives in a slum or a small rented room. He is usually poorly dressed and poorly fed. A rickshaw puller works very hard from morning till night. He carries passengers from one place to another in exchange for money. He pulls his rickshaw in the sun and rain and often has to wait for passengers. A rickshaw puller faces many problems in his life. His income is small and uncertain. He suffers a lot when he falls ill or when there are few passengers. His body becomes weak because of hard labour and poor food. Yet a rickshaw puller is very useful to us. He carries us quickly and cheaply through the narrow lanes. So, we should be kind to him and pay him his fair fare.

data.prompt_en: Write a paragraph about 'Load Shedding' answering: (a) What is load shedding? (b) Why does it happen? (c) How does it affect students? (d) How does it affect industry? (e) How can it be reduced?
data.model_answer_en: Load shedding means the sudden stoppage of the supply of electricity for some time. It is a common problem in our country, especially in summer. Load shedding happens when the demand for electricity is greater than its production. System loss, misuse of power and the shortage of power plants are the main causes behind it. Load shedding affects the students most. They cannot study at night in the darkness and become worried about their examinations. It also does great harm to our industry. Mills and factories stop working during load shedding, so the production of goods falls and the country suffers a great loss. Load shedding can be reduced in several ways. We should not waste electricity and must use energy-saving bulbs. The government should build more power plants and stop the illegal use of electricity. If we all become careful, this problem can be solved.

data.prompt_en: Write a paragraph about 'A Nurse' answering: (a) Who is a nurse? (b) Where does she work? (c) What does she do? (d) What qualities should she have? (e) How important is she?
data.model_answer_en: A nurse is a woman who looks after the sick and the wounded. She is an important member of the medical profession. A nurse works in hospitals, clinics and health centres. Sometimes she also serves patients at their homes. Her main duty is to take care of the patients. She gives them medicine in time, feeds them and keeps them clean and comfortable. She helps the doctors during operations and follows their instructions carefully. A nurse should have some special qualities. She should be kind, patient, sincere and dutiful. She must love her patients and serve them like her own relatives. Florence Nightingale set a bright example of a devoted nurse. The service of a nurse is very important to us. She brings comfort to the suffering people and helps them recover. So, we should honour and respect nurses for their noble service.
